learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic concepts related to corporate investment and financing decisions, separation of ownership and control, and corporate governance objectives.

Acquire basic accounting principles: balance sheet and income statement formation, statutory balance sheet scheme and reclassification, accounting systems and methods of accounting, revenues and monetary assets, inventories and cost of goods sold, fixed assets and depreciation, liabilities and equity, financial statement analysis.
Acquire basic concepts of management accounting: direct and indirect costs, budget and management control.
Be able to apply methodologies for investment analysis, read and analyze financial statements, and prepare sales, production, and cash budgets.

Be able to interpret corporate financial data, including profitability, liquidity, solvency, and operational efficiency indicators. Develop skills for evaluating the financial health of companies, identifying strengths and weaknesses through financial statement analysis.
Improve communication skills with people outside the academic environment through interaction with industry professionals or corporate stakeholders during guest speaker seminars.
Strengthen learning abilities, allowing for further self-study of business economics topics.

syllabus_topics: Corporate finance, business objectives and corporate governance
The balance sheet as a tool for management analysis and economic-financial results
Project management: time, costs, and risk
assessment_rules: The assessment includes a written exam and a possible oral discussion. The written exam may include multiple-choice questions (+1 point for a correct answer, -0.5 for an incorrect answer, 0 for no answer) and open-ended questions on theoretical topics.
